connection_condition: superhero.publisher_id corresponds to publisher.id; a publisher is an independent entity that exists without any hero, so the link is a reference rather than a whole-part structure.
description: Each superhero record carries at most one publisher attribution, while a publisher holds many heroes. Roster analysis aggregates from heroes up to the publisher, and the attribution is incomplete for some records.
A superhero is classified into one alignment category. Alignment is a shared classification list, not a component of the hero record.
A superhero is classified into one gender category from a shared list that also contains an unrecorded category.
A superhero is assigned one species or origin category from a shared list that includes an explicit unspecified entry and may be absent entirely.

connection_condition: superhero.eye_colour_id, superhero.hair_colour_id and superhero.skin_colour_id each correspond to colour.id, so three distinct appearance attributes of the same hero resolve against one shared colour list.
description: Appearance colours of a superhero are drawn from a single shared colour vocabulary. Because one vocabulary serves three attributes, a colour label alone does not identify which appearance attribute it describes.

connection_condition: hero_power associates superhero.id with superpower.id; both sides of the association are independent entities and no ownership exists in either direction.
description: A superhero possesses many named abilities and a named ability is shared by many superheroes, giving a many-to-many association that cannot be expressed as a column of the hero record.

connection_condition: hero_attribute.hero_id corresponds to superhero.id; a rating row has no meaning without the hero it rates.
description: The capability ratings of a superhero are components of that hero's profile: removing the hero record leaves its ratings meaningless, and each hero carries exactly one rating per dimension.

connection_condition: hero_attribute.attribute_id corresponds to attribute.id, selecting which of the six dimensions a rating expresses.
description: Each rating is expressed on exactly one attribute dimension, and a dimension is realised through the ratings of many heroes. The dimension supplies the meaning of the numeric value rather than being a part or a supertype of it.

connection_condition: Derived by counting the distinct powers associated with one hero in hero_power; no stored column holds the result.
description: The breadth of a hero's abilities is derived from the set of powers associated with that hero rather than being stored directly.

connection_condition: Derived by counting superhero records grouped by their publisher reference; no stored column holds the result.
description: The size of a publisher's roster is derived from the number of superhero records attributed to that publisher, so it changes whenever the attribution of a hero changes.

connection_condition: superhero.id is the authoritative value of the identifier, and hero_attribute.hero_id and hero_power.hero_id reuse the same value domain to reference a hero.
description: The hero identifier denotes a superhero record and is the value through which dependent records attach to it. Its representations differ only by column naming convention across tables.
